newsitem.title: USA: US corporate bonds firm before US West unit's deal.
newsitem.headline: US corporate bonds firm before US West unit's deal.

text.p: U.S. investment grade corporate bond spreads were steady to firmer on Wednesday amid some big new issuance and the promise of more supply in grand proportions from a US West Inc unit on Thursday, dealers said.
In high-yield issues, traders said the first of what is expected to be more than $5.0 billion in new supply through February sold easily, and traded higher by the market close.

Back in high-grades, fixed-income market participants were bracing for Thursday's giant $3.5 billion debt offering from US West Capital Funding, a unit of US West Inc. The issue was increased in size on Wednesday from a planned $2.0 billion.

High-yield issues featured $150 million of 9-3/4 percent senior subordinated notes of 2008 from Del Webb Corp, priced to yield 9.825 percent via lead manager Dillon Read & Co. The issue was seen trading as high as 100-1/4 at the close.

Traders stressed high-yield market fundamentals remain intact despite the propects of heavy supply in the near term. "Double-B paper gets affected a little with Treasuries down but overall our market continues to tighten," a trader said. "Our technicals haven't changed -- we're still at the tip of the iceberg as far as new issuance but (the market) feels strong."
